raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Overview

Make a too-old NCCL for DeepEP v2 self-explanatory on pip/uv installs. PyTorch pins an NCCL older than the 2.30.4 that `--all2all-backend deepep_v2` needs (PyTorch 2.13 pins `nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.29.7`). The Docker images override it since #45321, but installs outside the images fail with a message that states the requirement and not the fix. This does not change any dependency.

## Claims

- The startup log line and the `DeepEPV2All2AllManager` assertion now name the cause and the upgrade command for the installed CUDA major.
- `tools/ep_kernels/install_python_libraries.sh` warns, before and after the build output, when the installed NCCL is too old for DeepEP v2. It does not fail, so DeepEP v1 builds are unaffected.
- `tools/ep_kernels/README.md` reflects the current PyTorch pin, explains that later `uv pip install` runs restore it without `UV_OVERRIDE`, and that DeepEP must be rebuilt after upgrading NCCL.

## Validation

On an environment with torch 2.13.0, `nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.29.7`, and DeepEP 2.0.0:

```console
$ python -c "from vllm.utils.import_utils import deep_ep_v2_unavailable_reason as r; print(r())"
DeepEP v2 requires NCCL >= 2.30.4 but found 2.29.7. PyTorch pins an older NCCL; upgrade it with `pip install "nvidia-nccl-cu13>=2.30.4" --no-deps` and rebuild DeepEP against it. See tools/ep_kernels/README.md.
```

The NCCL check from the install script, run in isolation against the same environment:

```console
WARNING: nvidia-nccl-cu13 2.29.7 is installed, but the deepep_v2 backend
requires NCCL >= 2.30.4 when DeepEP is built and when it runs. To use deepep_v2, run
    uv pip install "nvidia-nccl-cu13>=2.30.4" --no-deps
and then run this script again. See tools/ep_kernels/README.md.
```

pre-commit (including shellcheck and markdownlint) and `mypy-3.12` pass on the changed files.

Not validated: the full install script was not re-run end to end, the Docker build was not run (it sets `UV_OVERRIDE`, so the warning should not trigger there), and the available path (NCCL >= 2.30.4) was not exercised on a real environment. No tests were added; the change is message text plus a shell warning.

## Details

`has_deep_ep_v2()` now delegates to a new `deep_ep_v2_unavailable_reason()`, so the log line and the assertion share one message. One behavior difference: an environment with a pre-v2 DeepEP installed now also gets the one-time INFO line saying `deepep_v2` is unavailable.

The alternative of forcing a newer NCCL through `[tool.uv] override-dependencies` in `pyproject.toml` was left out on purpose to avoid changing dependencies.

Not a duplicate: searches for `deepep_v2 NCCL` and `nccl install_python_libraries` found no open PR addressing this.

AI assistance was used to investigate and implement this change.

---

+## NCCL version requirement for DeepEPv2
 
-DeepEPv2 uses the NCCL GIN (GPU-Initiated Networking) backend, which requires
-NCCL >= 2.30.4 at both compile time and runtime. PyTorch 2.11 pins
-`nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.28.9` as a transitive dependency, so you need to
-override it.
+DeepEPv2 (`--all2all-backend deepep_v2`) uses the NCCL GIN (GPU-Initiated
+Networking) backend, which requires NCCL >= 2.30.4 both when DeepEP is built
+and at runtime. PyTorch pins an older release as a dependency (PyTorch 2.13
+pins `nvidia-nccl-cu13==2.29.7`), so a plain `pip install` or `uv pip install`
+of vLLM is not enough. The vLLM Docker images already override it.
+
+Upgrade NCCL before running `install_python_libraries.sh`. Use
+`nvidia-nccl-cu12` on CUDA 12.
 
 **With uv** (recommended):
 
@@ -29,18 +33,22 @@ export UV_OVERRIDE=/tmp/nccl-override.txt
 uv pip install vllm
 ```
 
-**With pip**:
+Keep `UV_OVERRIDE` set for later installs into the same environment. Without
+it, any `uv pip install` that resolves PyTorch again restores the pinned NCCL.
+
+**With pip**, or to fix an existing environment:
 
 ```bash
-pip install vllm
 pip install "nvidia-nccl-cu13>=2.30.4" --no-deps
 ```
 
-The override / reinstall must happen before building DeepEP (for GIN device
-headers) and must remain in place at runtime. You can verify with:
+`install_python_libraries.sh` warns when the installed NCCL is too old. If
+DeepEP was built against an older NCCL, upgrade NCCL and run the script again.
+When NCCL is too old at runtime, vLLM logs the reason at startup and
+`deepep_v2` fails with the same message. You can check with:
 
 ```bash
-python -c "from vllm.utils.import_utils import has_deep_ep_v2; print(has_deep_ep_v2())"
+python -c "from vllm.utils.import_utils import deep_ep_v2_unavailable_reason; print(deep_ep_v2_unavailable_reason() or 'deepep_v2 is available')"
 ```
 
 ## Usage

@@ -78,10 +78,25 @@ mkdir -p "$WHEEL_DIR"
 pushd "$WORKSPACE"
 
 # install dependencies if not installed
+UV_PIP_TARGET=()
 if [ -z "$VIRTUAL_ENV" ]; then
-  uv pip install --system cmake torch ninja
-else
-  uv pip install cmake torch ninja
+  UV_PIP_TARGET=(--system)
+fi
+uv pip install "${UV_PIP_TARGET[@]}" cmake torch ninja
+
+# DeepEPv2 needs NCCL >= 2.30.4 at both build time and runtime, but PyTorch
+# pins an older release.
+DEEPEP_V2_MIN_NCCL="2.30.4"
+NCCL_PACKAGE="nvidia-nccl-cu${CUDA_VERSION_MAJOR}"
+NCCL_WARNING=""
+NCCL_INSTALLED=$(uv pip show "${UV_PIP_TARGET[@]}" "$NCCL_PACKAGE" 2>/dev/null | sed -n 's/^Version: //p')
+if [ -n "$NCCL_INSTALLED" ] && \
+    [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$DEEPEP_V2_MIN_NCCL" "$NCCL_INSTALLED" | sort -V | head -n1)" != "$DEEPEP_V2_MIN_NCCL" ]; then
+    NCCL_WARNING="WARNING: ${NCCL_PACKAGE} ${NCCL_INSTALLED} is installed, but the deepep_v2 backend
+requires NCCL >= ${DEEPEP_V2_MIN_NCCL} when DeepEP is built and when it runs. To use deepep_v2, run
+    uv pip install \"${NCCL_PACKAGE}>=${DEEPEP_V2_MIN_NCCL}\" --no-deps
+and then run this script again. See tools/ep_kernels/README.md."
+    echo "$NCCL_WARNING" >&2
 fi
 
 # fetch nvshmem
@@ -236,3 +251,8 @@ if [ "$MODE" = "wheel" ]; then
     echo "All wheels written to $WHEEL_DIR"
     ls -l "$WHEEL_DIR"
 fi
+
+# Repeat after the verbose build output, where the first copy is easy to miss.
+if [ -n "$NCCL_WARNING" ]; then
+    echo "$NCCL_WARNING" >&2
+fi
